A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same activation-transfer study and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices sufficient for comparison. Relocated material was matched, including v2 Appendix I becoming v3 Appendix K.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on backdoor removal, refusal transfer, corrupted capabilities, activation reconstruction, model switching and SAE feature transfer.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds humor steering, MediQA transfer, noise-control experiments and out-of-distribution evaluations.

M1.justification: Appendix I introduces an intervention adaptation for humor: a mapped steering direction derived from middle-layer activations is applied uniformly across all target-model layers. The core autoencoder architecture, affine alternative and training losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds humorous-response generation and curated MediQA medical question answering, plus AlpacaEval instruction-following evaluation (Appendices I, J and L). The OpenWebText examples used to interpret SAE features in v2 are removed. These changes substantially broaden coverage beyond the retained safety tasks.

E2.justification: Appendix H adds reconstruction-only and mapped-reconstruction-only baselines to the SAE transfer comparison, alongside explicit random-noise comparisons. These controls were absent from that experiment in v2, although noise comparisons existed elsewhere. Existing affine, native-steering and mean-ablation comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The SAE transfer evaluation changes from 1,000 prompts to 100, with feature scaling and a noise-conditioned success measure. Added protocols include 20 held-out humor prompts, a three-point MediQA judging rubric, reduced zero-shot MMLU using four questions per domain, and 100 AlpacaEval instructions. The original benchmark protocols remain documented separately.

E4.justification: v3 substantially revises the SAE analysis through reconstruction/mapping-noise controls, comparisons across features, scaling sensitivity and the Gaussian-noise sweep in Figure 24. It removes the old feature-activation examples and patching case study. New analyses examine humor-data sensitivity and out-of-distribution failures, including results restricted to non-backdoored outputs.

E5.justification: The new noise sweep specifies averaging ten random-noise samples per prompt and then averaging across 50 prompts. This adds a statistical estimation procedure, without establishing increased repetition of earlier experiments. The standard-deviation reporting in Table 27 is retained; no new confidence intervals or significance tests are supplied.

E6.justification: v2's SAE report of 83% source triggering, 80% target triggering and 94.22% conditional transfer is replaced by differently conditioned results. v3 reports 8%/63% reconstruction-only triggering and 81%/89% with factor-three feature scaling; these are not comparable performance gains. New results include approximately 60% humor success, a reported 7.14% MediQA improvement, and MMLU declines from 0.605 to 0.101 for Qwen and 0.373 to 0.004 for Llama after mapping.

T1.justification: The autoencoder equations, steering and projection definitions, and reconstruction-loss formulations in Section 3.3 and Appendices A and D are retained. v3 adds no formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims about cross-model intervention transfer, corrupted capabilities, lightweight behavioral switches and tokenizer-dependent cross-architecture transfer. The additional experiments do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Section 8 and Appendix L newly qualify activation replacement through severe out-of-distribution capability losses and unintended backdoor responses. Appendix H interprets feature-transfer effects relative to substantial reconstruction and mapping noise. Section 6 also removes v2's qualification that affine mappings were competitive for the Llama pair and its proposed distillation explanation.

D1.justification: v3 clarifies SAE patch timing and placement before Top-K activation, and supplies task-specific data preparation and judging details. Appendix J adds the MediQA generation prompt, dataset access information and fine-tuning settings: ten epochs, batch size three, learning rate 3e-5 and sequence length 512. Existing core configurations and repository links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The background adds explicit positioning against Lindsey et al.'s crosscoders and Lee et al. (2025a)'s linear steering transfer. New benchmark citations accompany MediQA, MMLU and AlpacaEval, while several background references are removed. Bibliographic updates to retained works do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: v3 edits the introduction and background, adds a roadmap, subdivides Appendix H, moves the steering sweep from C.1 to B.1, and condenses resource information into a footnote. The overall narrative remains recognizable, and the long completion appendix is unchanged apart from relocation and renumbering.

P2.justification: Main figures and tables are repositioned, Figure 24 and new judging-prompt boxes are added, and the old SAE example table and patching-example box are removed. The probe-accuracy table changes from Table 31 to Table 30 without changing its scores. Most existing displays retain their content.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important validation gaps: Appendix H quantifies reconstruction and mapping noise that could confound v2's SAE-transfer evidence, while Appendix L exposes previously untested capability losses and unintended backdoor activation. These changes substantially improve evidential rigor and clarify applicability. The smaller SAE sample, 20-prompt humor evaluation and still-broad headline claims limit the revision, but the added controls and explicit failure evidence provide a clear overall improvement.
